why: The smallest complete union-find: union the two ends of every edge, then source and destination are connected exactly when find gives the same root. With 2 * 10^5 vertices and edges, union by rank (or size) and path compression keep every operation nearly O(1).
hints: You only need to know whether two vertices end up in the same group, not the path between them.
Union-find: parent[v] starts as v; find follows parents to the root; union links one root under the other.

Add union by rank so trees stay shallow and path compression (point nodes at their grandparent or root during find). Union every edge, then compare find(source) and find(destination). O((n + E) alpha(n)).
pitfalls: source == destination is true even for an isolated vertex.
Without rank and compression, a chain of 2 * 10^5 unions makes find linear and the whole run quadratic.
